notes:
Need to search first.I couldn't write these notes because my research tools stopped working before I could read any sources.

1. My first try was to open five pages directly: Enduring Word's Proverbs 26 page, Precept Austin's Proverbs 26 commentary, the Bible Hub commentaries on 26:2 and 26:4, and the NET Bible notes. The tool blocked all five because it only opens addresses that have already come up in a search.
2. I then ran eight searches to get usable addresses, covering the chapter as a whole, verses 2, 4–5, 10, 11 and 12, and the NET Bible notes. The tool refused to run them and said I had no tool calls left for this turn.

So I haven't read a single page on Proverbs 26. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give the address for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Anything I wrote now would break those rules, so I haven't written any notes rather than give you unsourced ones.

**Next step:** if you send the request again (for example, "continue"), the tool limit should reset and I'll pick up from those searches. I'll keep the number of tool calls low by gathering the main verse-by-verse commentaries first (Enduring Word, Bible Hub's Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit, StudyLight, Precept Austin). Then I'll look up the verses where readers most often disagree: v. 4–5 (whether or not to answer a fool), v. 2 (the undeserved curse), v. 8 (a translation difficulty) and v. 10 (a hard Hebrew text with very different translations). After that I'll check NET Bible, Catholic and Orthodox sources, and the tradition-specific sites. You could also paste in commentary pages you already have, and I'll write the notes from those with their addresses.
